scope: REM-0301 inventory and classification; this file does not implement a backup format

path_variables.${SATURN_HOME}: Home directory of the configured Saturn operator account

entries.description: Hashed and plaintext administrator credential backends, initial-login recovery material, and a provisioning file that may contain SATURN_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
entries.restore_notes: Never copy to a different appliance. Prefer setting a new password with saturn-admin-password.sh after restore. Delete initial-login.txt after the operator records or changes the initial credential.

entries.description: Linux account password hashes and group credentials.
entries.restore_notes: Owned by whole-system recovery, not Saturn settings restore.

entries.description: Server-side HMAC secret used with the administrator credential to validate remembered-browser cookies. Browser cookies themselves live on each browser and are not appliance files.
entries.restore_notes: Omitting or regenerating this secret intentionally revokes remembered devices. Never transfer it to another appliance.

entries.description: Self-signed Saturn Remote certificate and private key.
entries.restore_notes: The certificate may be reported by subject, expiry, and fingerprint; the private key must never enter a support bundle. A new appliance should generate a new pair.

entries.description: Current UI, display, receiver, DSP, filter, EQ, CFC, microphone, drive, and transmit preferences.
entries.restore_notes: Portable when the destination radio supports the same capabilities. Review transmit drive, microphone gain, antenna, ADC, and filter choices before transmitting.

entries.description: Named startup, display, receiver, DSP, and transmit profiles.
entries.restore_notes: Portable with the same transmit-safety review required for current remote settings.

entries.description: piHPSDR radio, protocol, GPIO, remote, calibration, and operator property files stored in the application repository.
entries.restore_notes: Copy only property files, not the whole source tree. Review radio identity, IP/protocol selection, GPIO, PA calibration, drive, and antenna values on different hardware.

entries.description: deskHPSDR startup, protocol, radio, and calibration property files.
entries.restore_notes: Review XDMA/network protocol selection, radio identity, PA calibration, drive, and antenna values before use on another radio. Log and error files in the same directory are diagnostics, not settings.

entries.description: Registry, labels, categories, versions, and flags for browser-managed scripts.
entries.restore_notes: Restore together with the matching operator-authored script files.

entries.description: Operator-authored script content is mixed with installer-provided scripts and may embed credentials, hostnames, paths, or destructive commands.
entries.restore_notes: Use custom_scripts.json to select only operator-authored files. Packaged scripts are regenerated by install. Review content before moving it to another appliance.

entries.description: Version marker required to interpret managed Saturn Go settings.
entries.restore_notes: Must travel with settings and be validated against the destination release before restore.

entries.description: Detected CM generation, storage variant, XDMA role, front panel, LCD profile, UART/panel overlays, PA protection, ATU, and installation contract.
entries.restore_notes: Useful for diagnosis and same-device recovery. Re-detect on different hardware instead of restoring it blindly.

entries.description: Provisioning phase, image-factory, and first-boot bookkeeping.
entries.restore_notes: Do not copy sealed-image markers or phase completion records to another appliance.

entries.owner: Boot firmware and Saturn hardware configuration
entries.description: LCD, front-panel UART, USB host, I2C, GPIO power LED, kernel command line, and other board boot settings. Only one path pair normally exists.
entries.restore_notes: Restore only to the same board/display role after comparing distribution defaults. A malformed file can prevent boot.

entries.description: Local shutdown, deploy, release, activation-safety, and installation policy.
entries.restore_notes: Installer defaults are regenerable. Preserve only intentional local overrides and never enable release activation merely because another host did.

entries.description: Ethernet/Wi-Fi profiles and credentials, including Saturn Ethernet fallback configuration.
entries.restore_notes: Site-specific. Prefer recreating through NetworkManager. Never include PSKs or private network topology in an ordinary support bundle.

entries.description: Tailscale node identity, keys, coordination state, and serve configuration.
entries.restore_notes: Never clone this directory to another radio. A replacement appliance should authenticate as a new Tailscale node and reapply serve policy.

entries.description: Machine identity, hostname mapping, and SSH host private keys.
entries.restore_notes: Same-device recovery only. New or cloned appliances must generate unique machine and SSH identities; support output may contain hostname and public fingerprints, never private keys or machine-id.

entries.description: SSH private keys, GitHub OAuth data, Git credentials, registry tokens, and other developer access material.
entries.restore_notes: Back up separately with the operator's credential manager. These are not Saturn appliance state.

entries.description: Prepared/active/rollback transaction records, previous deployment snapshots, migration backups, and update results.
entries.restore_notes: Required to understand or complete recovery on the same appliance. Do not use another host's transaction record. Support copies should redact repository URLs if private repositories are later supported.

entries.description: Active source path and configured public repository/ref/update policy.
entries.restore_notes: Repository paths are host-specific. Revalidate owner, repository, ref, and local path on restore.

entries.description: Root-owned immutable application releases and the active release pointer.
entries.restore_notes: Prefer reinstalling the exact signed/validated release. Support output needs commit, manifest, hashes, and pointer target rather than binaries.

entries.description: Mutable source trees, update-script repository copies, and source backups. Local uncommitted changes are the only irreplaceable portion.
entries.restore_notes: Record remotes, commits, dirty status, and patch files. Existing Saturn Go full backup and script backups are repository copies, not appliance backups.

entries.description: Inactive staging worktrees, snapshots, dependency trees, compiler outputs, and native build caches.
entries.restore_notes: Recreate instead of restoring. Support output may report size and commit only.

entries.description: Provisioning, update, application, and system logs.
entries.restore_notes: Never restore logs as settings. A support bundle may include bounded, sanitized excerpts after removing credentials, tokens, private addresses when requested, and user-entered script output.

entries.description: Repository FPGA images/sources are reproducible artifacts; the image actually flashed in hardware is external device state and is not captured by a Saturn settings backup.
entries.restore_notes: Record reported FPGA version/date and selected image checksum. Defining authoritative FPGA artifact and readback policy remains with the FPGA maintainers.

entries.description: Ephemeral enable flags and live performance/ADC telemetry.
entries.restore_notes: Never restore. A support bundle may take a sanitized point-in-time snapshot.
